purpose: Add selected physical science explanations, worked calculations and questions to the general learning material.
attribution: Selections adapted from Astronomy 2e by Andrew Fraknoi, David Morrison, Sidney C. Wolff, OpenStax at Rice University, and the contributors credited in the preserved original preface. Source: https://github.com/openstax/osbooks-astronomy/tree/9d7e69a2e0c9a651ad42254b9a93b701a6b08c10 . This pinned 2024 edition declares Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . The original license and preface are retained beside the prepared text. Changes: CNXML converted to text; MathML serialized as LaTeX; local figure/table/equation/example references renumbered; merged table cells expanded; images represented by their source descriptions with captions and credits retained; front/back matter, specified sidebars and one malformed chapter-review module omitted; exact substantial duplicate paragraphs removed. No endorsement by OpenStax or the authors is implied. The repository MIT license applies to code and does not replace the source text license. Two explicit source errata correct Cassini's Jupiter flyby year and the orbital origin of gravity-assist energy, with NASA references retained in the selection.

excluded_modules.reason: Chapter review contains a table declaring two columns but a heading spanning an undeclared third column. Deferred instead of silently repairing the source.

split_policy: Whole chapter 17 is validation and whole chapter 19 is reserved test. All other selected chapters train. Exact normalized paragraphs of at least 120 characters are reserved for existing heldouts, then new test, then validation before training.
limitations: Sampled review, not an exhaustive scientific or editorial audit. The pinned 2024 text includes dated counts and mission descriptions; it is not a current astronomical database. Entire topics are held out, so validation/test entail topic shift. Exact paragraph removal does not eliminate shorter overlap, paraphrases, shared definitions or cross-references. Some source illustrations are described rather than seen. Thirty-three unresolved cross-references in the initial draft use generic text. No model has learned this edition yet; no native curriculum is created automatically.
